newsitem.title: USA: TCC Schumann resigns as chairman, CEO.
newsitem.headline: TCC Schumann resigns as chairman, CEO.

text.p: TCC Industries Inc said Monday that Lawrence Schumann had resigned as chairman, chief executive and president, and that Walter DeRoeck was elected to succeed Schumann as chairman and interim chief executive.

The company said Schumann had also agreed to resign from positions he held with TCC's subsidiaries. Additionally, the company said Robert Thomajan had been elected to replace Frank Denius, who resigned as company secretary.
A statement from the company did not provide a reason for Schumann's resignation, and a call to the company's offices in Austin, Texas, seeking further information was not immediately returned.
DeRoeck and Thomajan, two nominees of a shareholders committee, were elected to the company board in May.
The company, which designs and makes bulk material conveying and processing systems, reported a 1996 net loss of $0.56 per share, compared to a loss of $0.03 in fiscal 1995.

Its statement said Schumann had agreed to sell shares of TCC stock he beneficially owns to DeRoeck and Thomajan for a price equal to the average closing price for the company's shares for the past fifteen trading day period.
TCC shares closed Monday up 1/8 at 2-1/4.
The company said its board approved a resolution to expand the board size by two seats and had appointed a nominating committee to conduct a search for a permanent chief executive.
